mechaber/1:main: Laws of mustard into which flour has been mixed. Containing 1 seif: Mustard or other types of condiments that contain water—one may not put flour into them. And if one placed [flour] into the mustard, he must eat it immediately and must not leave it to stand, lest it become chametzed. And with other types of condiments, since they are not as sharp as mustard, it has certainly become chametzed and must be destroyed if it is after the time when chametz becomes forbidden. {Rama: And the custom is not to eat mustard at all on Passover, even if it was mixed before Passover, for it is like types of legumes which people customarily forbid. (Hagahot Maimoniyot ch. 5 and Terumat HaDeshen siman 112)}
baer-heitev/1:א: (1) Water—for if not so it would be fruit juice and they do not cause chametzing, even though they are sour things in themselves, as stated in siman 462 seif 1.
baer-heitev/1:ב: (2) Mixed—meaning they make it with wine, crush it, and grind it until it is not recognizable (Terumat HaDeshen). And wine into which mustard was placed while still new, which preserves it in its sweetness—Rabbeinu Yerucham permitted it (and Maharil forbids it, for it is a substance that causes chametzing, and even if one could leave it to stand they do not permit it; see Chayei Adam) to leave it in the house but not to drink. And Taz wrote in the name of Rokeach that they eat mustard on Passover only that it should not be ground in a chametz bowl—end of his words.
beer-hagolah/1:_: Mishnah Pesachim 40, and as Tosafos, and as Rav Kahana explains it.
machatzit-hashekel/1:א: (s.k. 1) Even if mixed—meaning they make it, etc.; do not err that mixed means with flour, for in that it is obvious it is forbidden whether mixed before Passover or on Passover; rather it means mixed with wine. And the novelty that even though at mixing they crush it and it does not appear like legumes when Passover enters, nevertheless it is forbidden. Nevertheless b'dieved if mustard fell into a dish it does not forbid; and also if mixed with wine without flour it is permitted to leave it, as Taz also wrote; and likewise mustard in its visible form is permitted to leave.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: And as above in siman 453 regarding legumes. And possibly Taz cited as a novelty mixed with wine is permitted to leave, for sometimes when mixing with wine they also put flour in it. Nevertheless when there is no flour in it, it is permitted to leave; and Maharshal wrote perhaps one might come to confuse.
magen-avraham/1:_: Even if mixed—meaning they make it with wine, crush it, and grind it until it is not recognizable like legumes; nevertheless it is forbidden (Terumat HaDeshen).
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) Other types of condiments—with which one dips meat, and they contain vinegar and other things that have acidity, and people are accustomed to put flour in them, for flour also becomes chametzed through acidity.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (2) That contain water—for if they have no water at all they are fruit juice and do not cause chametzing, even though they are sour things in themselves, as written above in siman 462. And according to what Rama wrote above in siman 462 seif 4, that we are stringent with fruit juice alone as well—even if they have no water at all—only types of condiments made from wine vinegar with flour are also forbidden.
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (3) He must eat immediately—for the strength of mustard does not let it stand long before chametzing.
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (4) And must destroy it—not specifically burning, as explained above in siman 445.
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (5) And the custom, etc.—and the reason is because mustard is a thing that is preserved and is like legumes which people forbid [Levush].
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (6) Even if mixed, etc.—it does not mean mixed with flour, for in that it is obvious it is forbidden whether before Passover or on Passover; rather it means mixed with wine. And the novelty that even though at the time of mixing they crush it and it does not appear like legumes, when Passover enters it is nevertheless forbidden. Nevertheless b'dieved if mustard fell into a dish it does not forbid it. And likewise it is permitted to leave mustard until after Passover since it is without flour. And wine into which mustard was placed while still fermenting so that it stands in its sweetness and does not spoil—it is permitted to leave it, but not to drink it.
turei-zahav/1:_: Even if mixed before Passover—this is l'chatchila; but b'dieved it does not forbid the dish, and likewise it is permitted to leave it until after Passover if one has mustard made for dipping without flour, for there is no chametzing in it at all, only a mere stringency. And Rokeach wrote in his work that they eat mustard on Passover only that it should not be ground in a chametz bowl.
